breathing_cue: Exhale as you row, inhale as you extend
coaching_cues: Chest on pad
pull handles toward the lower abdomen, elbows close to the body
Retract scapulae at the back of the movement — squeeze shoulder blades together
Controlled full stretch forward — don't lose the mid-back tension
common_mistakes: Shrugging the traps instead of retracting the scapulae
Bouncing out of the stretched position — slow, controlled eccentric
Pulling too high — row to navel, not to chest
warmup_protocol: 1×15 light for shoulder and mid-back activation
pro_tip: Closer neutral grip hits the mid-back rhomboids and traps harder; wider pronated grip shifts emphasis to the lats. Use both across your training week

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
breathing_cue: Exhale as you push the bar down toward your thighs
coaching_cues: Arms stay straight the ENTIRE movement — this is NOT a lat pulldown
Hinge slightly at the hips
pull the bar in a sweeping arc from overhead to thighs
Think 'armpits to pockets' — this movement is pure lat without bicep interference
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows — converts to a lat pulldown and removes the isolation
Using too much weight and swinging the torso
Not reaching full overhead stretch at the start
warmup_protocol: 1×15 very light to feel the lat-shoulder connection
pro_tip: Best pure lat isolation exercise — zero bicep involvement. If you want to feel your lats without bicep fatigue, this is it

name: Captain's Chair Leg Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you raise the legs, inhale on the lower
coaching_cues: Back flat against the pad
arms pressing down into the supports
Posterior pelvic tilt — tuck the pelvis BEFORE lifting
this switches hip flexors off
Raise knees to 90° for beginner
straight-leg raise for advanced
common_mistakes: Swinging the legs with momentum — slow controlled reps only
Not tilting the pelvis — most of the work goes to hip flexors instead of abs
Lower back arching away from the pad
pro_tip: Add a twist at the top to target obliques — brings knee toward the opposite elbow at peak contraction

name: Flutter Kicks
breathing_cue: Breathe steadily throughout; exhale every few kicks
coaching_cues: Lie on back
lift both feet 6 inches off the floor
Alternate small quick kicks
lower back pressed firmly to the floor throughout
Point toes to keep tension on the core and hip flexors
common_mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor — reduces core demand and risks injury
Lifting feet too high — makes it easier
warmup_protocol: Not required; can be used as active warm-up
pro_tip: Lower Abs Superset: flutter kicks 30s → leg raise 10 reps → rest 60s. Devastating lower-abdominal burnout circuit

name: Side Plank
breathing_cue: Breathe slowly and steadily throughout the hold
coaching_cues: Elbow directly below the shoulder
body forms a straight diagonal line
Lift the hips high — do NOT sag
squeeze the oblique to keep the position
Stack feet or stagger them for stability
raise the top arm for extra challenge
common_mistakes: Hips sagging below the line — defeats the purpose
Neck craning upward — keep it neutral, in line with the spine
Elbow placed too far from under the shoulder — makes it unstable
warmup_protocol: Not required; great as an activation drill
pro_tip: Add a hip dip (controlled tap to the floor and back up) to make it dynamic — transforms a static hold into a loaded oblique movement

name: Wall Sit
breathing_cue: Breathe normally throughout the hold
coaching_cues: Feet shoulder-width apart
Back flat against wall
Thighs parallel to floor
Hold position
warmup_protocol: Light leg swings and bodyweight squats
pro_tip: Drive heels into floor to maintain position

name: Bodyweight Good Morning
breathing_cue: Inhale as you hinge forward, exhale as you return
coaching_cues: Hands behind head or on hips
Soft bend in knees
Hinge at hips, not waist
Feel stretch in hamstrings
warmup_protocol: Hip circles and dynamic leg swings
pro_tip: Focus on the hip hinge movement pattern to protect your lower back

name: Doorframe Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Stand in doorframe
Grip frame at hip height
Lean back at 45 degrees
Curl body up using biceps
pro_tip: Lean further back to increase difficulty

name: Towel Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Loop towel around a sturdy door handle
Lean back keeping body straight
Pull chest toward door
Squeeze shoulder blades at top
pro_tip: The further your feet are from the door, the harder the row

name: Negative Pull Up
breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower slowly
coaching_cues: Jump or step to top position
Start with chin above bar
Lower yourself as slowly as possible
5-10 seconds down
pro_tip: Control the eccentric to build pulling strength for full pull-ups

name: Glute Kickback
breathing_cue: Exhale as you kick back, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: On hands and knees
Keep core tight
Kick leg back and up
Squeeze glute at top
pro_tip: Add ankle weight or resistance band to increase difficulty

name: Dumbbell Calf Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you rise, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Hold dumbbells at sides
Rise on balls of feet
Full range at top and bottom
Control the descent
warmup_protocol: Ankle rotations and light calf stretches
pro_tip: Stand on a step edge for greater range of motion

name: Split Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you rise
coaching_cues: Staggered stance, rear foot elevated or flat
Lower back knee toward floor
Keep front shin vertical
Drive through front heel to rise
common_mistakes: Rising on toes of front foot
warmup_protocol: Hip flexor stretches and leg swings
pro_tip: Elevate rear foot on a bench to increase range (Bulgarian split squat)

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
breathing_cue: Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Set bench to 30-45 degree incline
Press dumbbells up and slightly together
Control the descent
Full range of motion at bottom
warmup_protocol: Arm circles and light dumbbell presses
pro_tip: Keep a slight arch in lower back for shoulder safety

name: Bodyweight Rear Delt Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie face-down on the floor or a bench
Arms out to the sides in a T, thumbs up
Squeeze shoulder blades to lift the arms
Keep the neck neutral and chin tucked
common_mistakes: Using momentum to swing the arms
Lifting the chest off the floor
pro_tip: Go light and slow — the rear delts respond to the squeeze, not the load

name: Elevated Pike Push Up
breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you press away
coaching_cues: Feet on a chair, sofa or low step
hips stacked high over the shoulders
Head travels toward the floor between the hands, not forward
Elbows track back at roughly 45 degrees, not flared wide
Press until the elbows lock, keeping the hips high throughout
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drop into a plank, which turns it into a push-up
Looking forward and craning the neck
Using a surface so high the wrists cannot stay flat
pro_tip: The higher the feet, the closer this gets to a handstand push-up. Raise the surface before you add reps.

name: Prone Reverse Snow Angel
breathing_cue: Breathe steadily; do not hold your breath at the top
coaching_cues: Lie face-down, forehead resting on the floor
Arms start by the hips, palms facing down
Sweep the arms out and overhead just above the floor, then back
Keep the arms straight and the ribs down the whole way
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest and arching the lower back to help the arms
Bending the elbows as the arms pass shoulder height
Rushing. The whole point is the slow sweep.
pro_tip: If the arms will not pass the shoulders, stop there. The range comes back as the mid-back wakes up.

name: Table Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie under a sturdy table and grip the edge at chest width
Body straight from heel to head, heels on the floor
Pull the chest to the underside of the table
Lower under control until the arms are straight
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag so the pull becomes a shrug
Using a light folding table that tips. Check it takes your weight first.
Pulling with the arms and never squeezing the shoulder blades
pro_tip: Bend the knees to make it easier, or put the heels on a chair to make it harder.

name: Prone Lat Pull
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull the elbows down, inhale as you reach
coaching_cues: Lie face-down with the arms straight overhead in a Y
Lift the hands slightly off the floor and hold them there
Pull the elbows down and back toward the ribs, squeezing the lats
Reach the arms overhead again without letting the hands touch down
common_mistakes: Resting the hands on the floor between reps, which kills the tension
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Arching the lower back instead of moving at the shoulder
pro_tip: This is the vertical pull you can do on a hotel floor. Squeeze for a full second at the bottom.

name: Sliding Lat Pull
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull yourself forward
coaching_cues: Kneel on a smooth floor with both hands on a folded towel in front of you
Slide the towel forward until the arms are overhead and the chest is low
Pull the towel back toward the knees using the lats, not the hips
Keep the ribs down so the lower back does not take over
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drop and the back arch at full reach
Pushing back with the legs instead of pulling with the lats
Trying it on carpet, where the towel will not slide
pro_tip: Reach only as far as you can keep the ribs down. The range grows with the mid-section, not the shoulder.

name: Doorway Isometric Lat Pull
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Stand in a doorway and reach both hands high onto the frame
Pull down and in against the frame as if driving the elbows to the ribs
Build to full effort over two seconds, then hold
Keep the shoulders down and away from the ears
common_mistakes: Jerking into full force instead of building into it
Holding the breath, which spikes blood pressure
Hanging off the frame rather than pulling against it
pro_tip: An isometric builds the mind-muscle link a beginner is missing. It is how you start owning your own bodyweight overhead.

name: Self-Resisted Bicep Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Place the free hand on top of the working wrist
Curl the working arm up while the free hand pushes back against it
Resist hard on the way down. The lowering is where the work is.
Keep the working elbow pinned to the ribs
common_mistakes: Pushing so hard nothing moves. It should still travel.
Letting the working elbow drift forward
Giving up the resistance on the lowering half
pro_tip: Go easy on the way up and fight hard on the way down. The negative is what a bodyweight curl has to offer.

name: Towel Bicep Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Stand on one end of a towel and hold the other in one hand
Curl upward while pressing down through the standing foot
Keep the elbow tight to the ribs and the wrist neutral
Lower slowly against the same tension
common_mistakes: Leaning back to help the arm up
Letting the towel go slack at the bottom
Gripping so hard the forearm fails before the bicep
pro_tip: Shorten your grip on the towel to increase the tension. It is your load selector.

name: Self-Resisted Triceps Extension
breathing_cue: Exhale as you extend, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: Working arm overhead, hand behind the head
Free hand grips the working wrist and resists as you straighten the arm
Keep the working elbow pointing at the ceiling, close to the head
Resist on the way back down as well
common_mistakes: Letting the working elbow flare out to the side
Only resisting on the way up
Shrugging the shoulder to get the arm overhead
pro_tip: If the shoulder will not let the arm sit overhead, do it with the arm across the chest instead.

name: Wall Triceps Extension
breathing_cue: Exhale as you press away from the wall
coaching_cues: Stand an arm-length from a wall, forearms flat against it, elbows at shoulder height
Body straight from heel to head
lean in until the forehead nears the wall
Press back to straight arms using the triceps only
Keep the elbows pointing forward, never flaring out
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows drift wide, which hands the work to the chest
Bending at the hips instead of holding a straight line
Standing too close, which removes most of the range
pro_tip: Step the feet further back to make it harder. This is the wall version of a skull crusher.

name: Prone Y Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie face-down, arms overhead in a Y, thumbs pointing up
Raise the arms as high as the shoulder blades allow
Keep the forehead down and the neck long
Lower slowly rather than dropping
common_mistakes: Lifting the head and compressing the neck
Shrugging the traps to get the arms higher
Arching the lower back to fake the range
pro_tip: Height is not the goal. A low, controlled raise with the traps quiet beats a high one with them loud.

name: Towel Lateral Raise
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Hold a towel taut in front of you at hip height, one end in each hand
Pull outward against the towel and raise the arms to shoulder height
Hold the outward tension for the whole set
Keep the shoulders down and the elbows soft
common_mistakes: Letting the towel go slack at the top
Raising above shoulder height, which brings the traps in
Holding the breath during the isometric
pro_tip: Widen your grip on the towel for less tension, narrow it for more.

name: Prone T Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie face-down, arms straight out to the sides in a T
Thumbs up
lift the arms by squeezing the shoulder blades together
Hold the top for a full second before lowering
Keep the forehead down and the ribs on the floor
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest to make the arms travel further
Shrugging the traps up toward the ears
Bending the elbows once it gets hard
pro_tip: If you can hold the top for a second, the mid-back is doing it. If you cannot, the momentum was.

name: Doorway Isometric Row
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Stand facing a doorway and grip both sides of the frame at chest height
Lean the hips back until the arms are straight and the body is angled
Pull the chest toward the frame and hold at the top
Squeeze the shoulder blades together for the whole hold
common_mistakes: Standing too upright, which removes the load
Pulling with the arms while the shoulder blades stay still
Letting the hips sag forward out of the straight line
pro_tip: Walk the feet forward to increase the lean and the difficulty.

name: Standing Towel Pull Apart
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull the towel apart
coaching_cues: Hold a towel taut at shoulder height, hands wider than the shoulders
Pull outward against the towel and draw the hands apart and back
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the end of the pull
Return slowly, keeping the towel under tension throughout
common_mistakes: Letting the towel go slack between reps
Arching the lower back to get more range
Leading with the hands instead of the shoulder blades
pro_tip: This is the band pull-apart for people who own no band. Narrow the grip for more tension.

name: Prone W Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie face-down with the elbows bent, arms forming a W beside the ribs
Drive the elbows back and up, squeezing the shoulder blades down
Keep the wrists in line with the forearms
Lower slowly without resting the arms on the floor
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows drift up toward the head, which recruits the traps
Lifting the chin and compressing the neck
Resting between reps, which kills the tension
pro_tip: The W hits the lower traps harder than the T. Alternate them week to week.

name: Towel Lat Pulldown
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you reach up
coaching_cues: Hold a towel taut overhead, hands wider than the shoulders
Pull outward against the towel and bring it down behind the head
Drive the elbows toward the ribs, not just the hands down
Press back overhead against the same tension
common_mistakes: Letting the towel slacken, which removes all resistance
Bringing it down in front instead of behind, which becomes a shrug
Leaning back to fake the range
pro_tip: Keep pulling out on the towel the whole set. The tension is the load.

name: Wall Lat Press
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Stand side-on to a wall with the near arm straight and the palm flat on it
Press the palm DOWN the wall as if pulling yourself up past it
Feel the lat under the armpit engage and hold
Keep the shoulder pulled away from the ear
common_mistakes: Pressing into the wall rather than down it
Shrugging the shoulder up as effort rises
Holding the breath through the contraction
pro_tip: A wall is always there. This teaches the lat what to do before there is a bar to do it on.

name: Prone Lat Pull Hold
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Lie face-down with the arms overhead and the hands off the floor
Pull the elbows down to the ribs and HOLD there
Keep the chest lightly off the floor and the neck long
Squeeze as if trying to bend a bar down through the whole hold
common_mistakes: Letting the hands drop to the floor mid-hold
Arching hard through the lower back instead of the upper
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
pro_tip: The hold builds what the rep cannot: time under tension with nothing to hang from.

name: Towel Hammer Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Stand on one end of a towel, holding the other with a neutral (thumb-up) grip
Curl upward while pressing down through the standing foot
Keep the elbow pinned to the ribs and the thumb up throughout
Lower slowly against the same tension
common_mistakes: Rotating the palm up, which turns it back into a standard curl
Leaning back to help the arm
Letting the towel go slack at the bottom
pro_tip: The neutral grip shifts the work to the brachialis, which is what adds width to the arm.

name: Doorway Isometric Curl
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Stand in a doorway with the elbow bent to 90 degrees and the palm under the frame
Press up into the frame as if curling it, building over two seconds
Keep the elbow tight to the ribs and the wrist neutral
Hold at full effort, then release slowly
common_mistakes: Jerking into full force instead of building into it
Letting the shoulder rise to help the arm press
Holding the breath, which spikes blood pressure
pro_tip: Do one hold at 90 degrees and one just below it. An isometric only trains the angle you hold.

name: Table Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Sit under a sturdy table and grip its edge with palms facing you
Keep the elbows tight to the ribs and pull the chest up toward your hands
Drive with the biceps rather than the shoulder blades
Lower under control until the arms are straight
common_mistakes: Rowing with the back instead of curling with the arms
Using a table that tips. Check it takes your weight first.
Letting the elbows travel forward as you pull
pro_tip: Walk the feet out to make it harder, tuck them in to make it easier.

name: Towel Triceps Extension
breathing_cue: Exhale as you extend, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: Hold one end of a towel overhead, the other behind the back in the opposite hand
Straighten the top arm against the resistance of the bottom hand
Keep the top elbow pointing at the ceiling, close to the head
Let the bottom hand resist on the way back down as well
common_mistakes: Letting the top elbow flare out to the side
Pulling so hard with the bottom hand that nothing moves
pro_tip: The bottom hand is your weight stack. Ease off it to add reps, pull harder to add load.

name: Elevated Diamond Push Up
breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Hands in a diamond on a chair, step or low table
feet on the floor
Elbows stay close to the ribs, not flared out
Lower until the chest touches the hands
Press to a full lockout and squeeze the triceps
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows, which hands the work to the chest
Letting the hips sag out of the straight line
Using a surface that slides. Brace it against a wall.
pro_tip: The higher the hands, the easier it is. This is how you work toward a floor diamond push-up.

name: Wall Triceps Press
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Face a wall with the palms flat at chest height and the elbows bent
Press into the wall as if straightening the arms, without moving
Keep the elbows tucked toward the ribs, never flared
Build to full effort over two seconds and hold
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows, which turns it into a chest press
Leaning the body weight in instead of pressing with the arms
Holding the breath through the effort
pro_tip: Set the elbow angle before you press. The angle you hold is the angle you train.

name: Towel Front Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Hold a towel taut in front of the thighs, one end in each hand
Pull outward against it and raise the arms to shoulder height
Keep the elbows soft and the shoulders down
Lower slowly, holding the outward tension the whole way
common_mistakes: Swinging the towel up with the hips
Raising above shoulder height, which brings the traps in
Letting the towel slacken at the bottom
pro_tip: Narrow the grip for more tension. That is your only load selector here.

name: Wall Shoulder Slide
breathing_cue: Exhale as you slide up, inhale as you come down
coaching_cues: Stand with the back, head and both forearms flat against a wall
Slide the forearms up the wall without letting them lift off it
Keep the lower back close to the wall
do not let the ribs flare
Come down slowly to just below shoulder height
common_mistakes: Letting the wrists or elbows peel off the wall to get more range
Arching the lower back away from the wall
Shrugging the shoulders up at the top
pro_tip: Go only as high as the forearms stay on the wall. The lost range is the point, not the failure.

name: Isometric Lateral Raise
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Raise both arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height
Hold there with the palms down and the elbows soft
Keep the shoulders pulled down away from the ears
Hold until the shoulders burn, then lower slowly
common_mistakes: Letting the arms drift forward out of the side plane
Dropping the arms rather than lowering them
pro_tip: No load needed. The side delt is small enough that gravity and time are plenty.

name: Prone Shoulder Extension
breathing_cue: Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie face-down with the arms straight beside the hips, palms facing in
Lift the hands toward the ceiling, keeping the arms straight
Squeeze at the top with the shoulders pulled down
Lower slowly without letting the hands rest on the floor
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows to get the hands higher
Lifting the chest to add range
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
pro_tip: Small range, big squeeze. Two inches done properly beats six done with the back.

name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
breathing_cue: Exhale as you drive up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, one foot planted, the other leg extended
Drive through the planted heel until the hips are level with the knee and shoulder
Squeeze the glute hard at the top for a full second
Keep the hips square. Do not let the free side drop.
common_mistakes: Letting the free hip sag, which hides the weak side
Pushing through the toes instead of the heel
Arching the lower back at the top instead of squeezing the glute
pro_tip: If the hamstring cramps, walk the heel closer to the hips. That is a leverage problem, not a weakness.

name: Sliding Leg Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull the heels in
coaching_cues: Lie on your back on a smooth floor with both heels on a folded towel
Bridge the hips up and hold them there for the whole set
Slide the heels out until the legs are almost straight
Pull the heels back in using the hamstrings, hips staying high
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drop as the legs extend
Sliding out further than you can pull back
Trying it on carpet, where the towel will not slide
pro_tip: Cramping hamstrings mean the range was too long, not that you are done. Shorten it.

name: Elevated Single Leg Hip Thrust
breathing_cue: Exhale as you drive up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Upper back resting on a chair or sofa edge, one foot planted
Other leg tucked or extended
drive through the planted heel
Finish with the hips level and the ribs down, not flared
Lower under control until the hips are just off the floor
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top instead of squeezing the glute
Letting the planted foot drift too far forward, which recruits the hamstring
Using a surface that slides out from under you
pro_tip: The chair adds range the floor cannot. That range is where the glute actually grows.

name: Standing Single Leg Hinge
breathing_cue: Inhale as you hinge, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Stand on one leg with a soft knee, arms reaching forward
Hinge at the hip, sending the free leg straight back as a counterweight
Keep the back flat and the hips square to the floor
Stand by driving the hip forward, not by pulling with the back
common_mistakes: Rotating the free hip open, which turns it into a twist
Rounding the back to reach lower
pro_tip: Touch a wall with your fingertips for balance. Balance failing first hides how much hamstring you have.

name: Barbell Standing Ab Rollout
breathing_cue: Exhale as you roll out, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: Brace the abs and tuck the pelvis before rolling
Roll out only as far as your lower back stays flat
Pull back with the abs, not the hips
common_mistakes: Sagging lower back at full stretch
Hips piking up on the way back
pro_tip: Start from the knees or use a wall stop before going standing
indian_alternative: Ab wheel or towel slide on a smooth floor

name: Suspended Abdominal Fallout
breathing_cue: Exhale as you fall out, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: Hold the handles with arms straight, body in a plank
Lean forward letting arms travel overhead
Pull back with the abs, keeping the body rigid
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows during the fallout
pro_tip: Stand closer to the anchor to make it easier
indian_alternative: Towel slide fallout on a smooth floor

name: Dumbbell Standing Front Raise Above Head
breathing_cue: Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Raise both dumbbells forward and up until the arms are overhead
Keep the elbows soft and the ribs down
Lower slowly, no swing
common_mistakes: Using weights too heavy for the overhead range
pro_tip: Go lighter than a normal front raise because the range is longer
indian_alternative: Raise a pair of water bottles overhead

name: Side Lying Adductor Stretch
breathing_cue: Breathe slowly; exhale to ease deeper
coaching_cues: Lie on your side with the top leg bent and foot planted
Let the lower leg relax and ease the inner thigh open
Hold, then switch sides
pro_tip: Stay relaxed; the stretch should feel mild in the inner thigh
indian_alternative: Butterfly stretch seated on the floor

name: Kettlebell Advanced Windmill
breathing_cue: Inhale at the top, exhale as you hinge down
coaching_cues: Press the bell overhead and lock the arm
Push the hip out and hinge, eyes on the bell
Reach down the leg and return by squeezing the glute
common_mistakes: Bending the knees instead of hinging
Letting the overhead arm drift forward
pro_tip: Learn it with no weight, then a light bell, before going heavy
indian_alternative: Unweighted windmill with a broomstick

name: Kettlebell Single Arm Clean and Jerk
breathing_cue: Exhale sharply at the clean and again at the jerk
coaching_cues: Hike the bell back, then drive hips to clean it to the rack
Dip and drive the legs to launch the bell overhead
Lock out, then lower the bell back to the rack under control
common_mistakes: Arming the bell instead of using the hips
pro_tip: Master the single-arm clean and push press first
indian_alternative: Dumbbell clean and press

name: Barbell Clean and Press
breathing_cue: Brace before the pull; exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Pull the bar explosively from the floor, extending hips
Catch the bar on the shoulders in a front rack
Press overhead to lockout, then lower with control
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms instead of the hips
pro_tip: Practise the hang clean and strict press separately first
indian_alternative: Dumbbell clean and press

name: Standing Archer
breathing_cue: Exhale as you draw the bow, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: Stand tall, one arm reaching out in front
Draw the other elbow back as if pulling a bowstring
Keep shoulders down and the torso still, then switch
pro_tip: Move slowly; squeeze the shoulder blade at the end
indian_alternative: Band pull-apart if a band is available

name: Kettlebell Arnold Press
breathing_cue: Exhale on the press, inhale on the way down
coaching_cues: Start with the bell at chin height, palm facing you
Rotate the palm outward as you press overhead
Reverse the rotation as you lower
common_mistakes: Using too heavy a bell and losing the rotation
pro_tip: Hold the bell upside down (bottoms-up) for extra stability work
indian_alternative: Dumbbell Arnold press

name: Back Lever
breathing_cue: Breathe steadily; do not hold your breath
coaching_cues: Rotate backward into an inverted hang and extend the hips

pro_tip: Slow reps with a full stretch grow calves better than bouncing
indian_alternative: Calf raises on a stair edge

name: Staircase Calf Raise

coaching_cues: Stand with the balls of the feet on a stair edge and heels hanging
Pause one second at the top
Lower slowly into a full stretch
common_mistakes: Cutting the range of motion short
pro_tip: Slow reps with a full stretch grow calves better than bouncing
indian_alternative: Calf raises on a stair edge

name: Seated Calf Stretch

coaching_cues: Sit tall with both legs straight in front of you
Pull the toes toward you with your hand, keep the knee straight
Lean forward slightly until you feel the calf stretch
common_mistakes: Holding the breath or forcing the range
pro_tip: Hold 30-60 seconds; repeat on the other side

name: Standing Calf Stretch
breathing_cue: Breathe slowly and relax deeper on each exhale
coaching_cues: Rest one heel on a bench with the leg straight, then reach for the toes
Keep the back leg straight and the toes pointing forward
Lean forward gently until the calf stretches
common_mistakes: Holding the breath or forcing the range
pro_tip: Hold 30-60 seconds; repeat on the other side

name: Smith Chair Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale at the top and brace, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Set the bench behind you at about knee height
Sit back to the bench under control, chest up
Drive through the whole foot to stand
common_mistakes: Dropping onto the bench instead of lowering
pro_tip: Pause lightly on the bench, do not rock back and bounce

name: Assisted Chest Dip
breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press up
coaching_cues: Kneel on the pad and lean the torso forward
Lower until the upper arms are parallel to the floor
Press up to straight arms without shrugging
common_mistakes: Upright torso, which shifts work to the triceps
pro_tip: Reduce the assistance weight a little each week

name: Band Single Arm Twisting Chest Press
breathing_cue: Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Anchor the band behind you at chest height
Press one hand forward while rotating the palm down
Resist the band pulling your torso round
common_mistakes: Letting the torso twist with the band
pro_tip: Stagger the stance to stay stable while pressing one arm

name: Dumbbell Single Arm Decline Chest Press

coaching_cues: Lie on a decline bench with one dumbbell at the chest
Press straight up over the lower chest

pro_tip: Use lighter loads than the two-arm press; balance costs strength

name: Machine Decline Chest Press

Press down and forward until the arms are nearly straight

pro_tip: Control the return; do not let the stack slam

name: Machine Incline Chest Press

pro_tip: Good for upper chest volume with low skill demand

name: Resistance Band Seated Chest Press

Press both hands forward until the arms are straight

name: Barbell Front Squat

coaching_cues: Rest the bar on the front shoulders, elbows high

Drive up through the mid-foot
common_mistakes: Elbows dropping, letting the bar roll forward
Heels lifting or knees caving in
pro_tip: If wrist mobility is poor use a cross-arm grip or straps

name: Isometric Chest Squeeze

coaching_cues: Cross the forearms at chest height and press them into each other
Squeeze as hard as you can while keeping the shoulders down
Keep elbows level with the hands
pro_tip: Squeeze at about 70% effort for the full hold

name: Medicine Ball Supine Chest Throw
breathing_cue: Exhale sharply as you throw
coaching_cues: Lie on your back holding the ball at the chest
Throw straight up as fast as you can
Catch softly with bent elbows and repeat
common_mistakes: Throwing off-line so the ball drifts away
pro_tip: Use a light ball (2-4 kg); speed matters more than load

name: Assisted Chin Up
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Set the assistance so you can do 8+ clean reps
Grip underhand shoulder-width and pull the chest toward the bar
Lower fully with control
common_mistakes: Using too much assistance for too long
Shrugging and cutting the range short
pro_tip: Reduce the assistance weight a little each week

name: Standing Assisted Chin Up
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Stand on the assist platform and grip the handles, palms toward you
Chest up, pull the chin over the handles
Lower slowly, fully extending the arms
common_mistakes: Pushing off the assist so hard it does the whole rep
pro_tip: Use less assistance each week until you can do unassisted reps.

name: Close Grip Chin Up
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Grip underhand, hands about 10-15 cm apart
Pull until the chin clears the bar, elbows close
Lower to a full hang
pro_tip: Close grip biases the biceps; keep the shoulders packed

name: Narrow Neutral Grip Chin Up
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Grip parallel handles close together, palms facing in
Pull until the chin clears the handles
Lower to a full hang
common_mistakes: Cutting the range short at the bottom
pro_tip: Neutral grip is usually the most shoulder-friendly pull-up variant

name: Clamshell
breathing_cue: Exhale as you open the knee, inhale as you close
coaching_cues: Lie on your side, knees bent about 45 degrees, feet together
Open the top knee without rolling the pelvis back
Pause at the top, lower slowly
common_mistakes: Rolling the hips backward to lift higher
pro_tip: Add a mini band above the knees once 15 clean reps are easy

name: Dumbbell Clean
breathing_cue: Brace before the pull, exhale on the catch
coaching_cues: Start with a dumbbell in each hand by your feet, hips back, flat back
Extend hips and shrug explosively, then drop under
Catch at the shoulders with elbows forward and stand tall
common_mistakes: Curling the dumbbells with the arms
Rounding the back at the start
pro_tip: Learn the hang position with a light load first

name: Kettlebell Two Arm Clean
breathing_cue: Brace before the pull, exhale on the catch
coaching_cues: Hinge back and swing the bell between the legs
Snap the hips forward and pull the bell close to the body
Catch in the rack position with elbows tucked
common_mistakes: Letting the bell crash onto the forearm
Pulling with the arms instead of the hips
pro_tip: Keep the elbow tight to the body to avoid forearm bruising

name: Cocoons
breathing_cue: Exhale as you crunch, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, knees bent over the hips
Pull the knees in as you curl the shoulders up
Return slowly without letting the feet touch down
common_mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
Using momentum or hip flexors instead of the abs
pro_tip: Short, slow range with a hard squeeze beats high reps

name: Band Concentration Curl

Curl up without swinging and squeeze at the top

pro_tip: A strict, slow rep beats a heavy swung one here

pro_tip: Hold a doorframe for balance until the range improves

pro_tip: Hold 30-60 seconds; repeat on the other side

common_mistakes: Using body swing to move the weight
pro_tip: Use light weight and a 1-second squeeze

pro_tip: Short, slow range with a hard squeeze beats high reps

pro_tip: Short, slow range with a hard squeeze beats high reps

pro_tip: Short, slow range with a hard squeeze beats high reps

name: Dumbbell Cuban Press

coaching_cues: Row the dumbbells up to chest height, elbows high

Press overhead, then reverse the path with control

name: Barbell Single Leg Deadlift

coaching_cues: Hold the bar in front, soft knee on the standing leg
Hinge at the hip while the free leg extends behind
Keep hips level and back flat, then stand tall
pro_tip: Practise with dumbbells or bodyweight before the barbell

name: Cable Deadlift
breathing_cue: Brace and inhale at the top, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Stand over a low cable with a bar or rope handle
Push the hips back, flat back, lower the handle to the shins
Stand tall by driving the hips forward
pro_tip: The cable line pulls forward; keep the stack path close to the legs

name: Dumbbell Deadlift

coaching_cues: Dumbbells by your sides or in front of the shins, feet hip-width

common_mistakes: Sinking too deep and straining the shoulders
pro_tip: Bend the knees to make it easier, straighten them to progress

name: Tricep Dips Floor

Lift the hips and bend the elbows to lower

common_mistakes: Hands placed too far behind, straining the shoulders
pro_tip: Keep the hips close to the hands to protect the shoulders

name: Kettlebell Double Snatch

Snap the hips and pull the elbows high, punching through overhead

common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms instead of the hips

common_mistakes: Rounding the back instead of hinging
pro_tip: Learn the windmill unloaded, then with a light bell

name: Cable Up Down Twist
breathing_cue: Exhale as you rotate, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: Stand sideways to the cable, handle held with both hands
Rotate the torso and sweep the handle across the body, up or down
Keep the hips square and control the return
common_mistakes: Using the arms instead of the torso
pro_tip: Pivot the back foot so the lower back is not twisted

name: Barbell Drag Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Keep the bar in contact with the body and drag it up
Pull the elbows back as the bar rises
Squeeze, then lower along the same path
common_mistakes: Letting the bar drift away from the body
pro_tip: Drag curls reduce front-delt help and bias the long head

name: Cable Drag Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Pull the elbows back as the handle rises along the body
Squeeze at the top
Lower along the same path
common_mistakes: Letting the cable drift away from the body
pro_tip: Drag curls reduce front-delt help and bias the long head

name: Elbow Dips
breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you press up
coaching_cues: Hold parallel bars, torso fairly upright
Keep elbows tight to the ribs on the way down
Press up until elbows fully lock out
common_mistakes: Dropping too deep and overloading the shoulders
pro_tip: Do bench dips first if you cannot do 8 clean reps
indian_alternative: Two sturdy chairs placed side by side

name: Dumbbell Lying Elbow Press
breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you extend
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, dumbbells over chest
Keep upper arms still, only forearms move
Press up until arms are straight
common_mistakes: Letting the weights drift toward the face fast
pro_tip: Start light: this hits the long head and stresses elbows
indian_alternative: Two water bottles or filled bags

name: Elliptical Trainer
breathing_cue: Breathe rhythmically with the stride
coaching_cues: Stand tall, hands on the moving handles
Push through the whole foot each stride
Keep a steady rhythm, no hanging on the rails
pro_tip: Alternate 1 min hard with 2 min easy for intervals

name: Chair Leg Extended Stretch
breathing_cue: Breathe slowly, exhale as you fold forward
coaching_cues: Sit tall on the edge of a chair, one leg extended straight out in front
Hinge from the hips with a flat back
Hold, then switch legs
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the toes
pro_tip: Pull toes toward you to add a gentle calf stretch

name: Resistance Band Leg Extension
breathing_cue: Exhale as you extend the knee
coaching_cues: Sit on a bench or chair, band looped around both lower legs
Straighten the knee fully and squeeze the quad
Return slowly to the start
common_mistakes: Leaning back to cheat the last reps
pro_tip: Pause 1 second at the top for a harder squeeze
indian_alternative: Dupatta or tied cloth strip anchored low is a weak substitute

name: Dumbbell Cross Face Lying Extension
breathing_cue: Exhale as you extend the elbow
coaching_cues: Lie back, dumbbell held over the shoulder
Lower it across the face toward the opposite shoulder
Extend the elbow back up to lockout
common_mistakes: Letting the upper arm drift out of position
Using a weight too heavy to control near the face
pro_tip: Keep the upper arm still; only the elbow bends

name: EZ Bar Decline Close Grip Face Press
breathing_cue: Inhale as the bar lowers, exhale as you extend
coaching_cues: Lie on a decline bench, EZ bar over chest
Bend only at the elbows to lower toward the forehead
Press back up without flaring the elbows
common_mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the forehead
pro_tip: Use a spotter or light weight, the bar travels near your face

name: Upward Facing Dog
breathing_cue: Inhale as you lift the chest, exhale to settle
coaching_cues: Lie face down, hands beside the ribs
Press up, straighten arms, lift thighs off the floor
Open the chest, shoulders away from the ears
common_mistakes: Dumping weight into the lower back
pro_tip: Keep glutes lightly engaged to protect the lower back

name: Farmers Walk
breathing_cue: Breathe steadily and stay braced
coaching_cues: Stand tall with a heavy dumbbell in each hand
Keep shoulders back and ribs down
Take short, quick steps in a straight line
pro_tip: Grip as hard as you can; it builds the forearms too

name: Kettlebell Figure 8
breathing_cue: Breathe steadily through each pass
coaching_cues: Stand wide, hinge with a flat back
Pass the kettlebell between and around the legs in a figure 8
Keep your chest up and hips low
common_mistakes: Dropping the bell when handing it off
pro_tip: Start with a light bell until the hand-offs feel smooth

name: Dumbbell Finger Curls
breathing_cue: Exhale as the fingers curl in
coaching_cues: Sit with forearms resting on thighs, palms up
Let the dumbbell roll to the fingertips
Curl the fingers closed, then the wrist
common_mistakes: Using heavy weight and losing the dumbbell
Lifting the forearms off the thighs
pro_tip: Pair with wrist curls for complete forearm work
indian_alternative: Heavy filled bucket handle or water can

name: Barbell Finger Curls
breathing_cue: Breathe normally throughout
coaching_cues: Sit with the forearms resting on the thighs, palms up
Let the bar roll to the fingertips, then curl the fingers closed
Squeeze hard at the closed position
common_mistakes: Letting the wrist bend and help
pro_tip: Start light because a heavy bar rolls out of the hands.

name: Flag
breathing_cue: Hold a shallow breath, exhale when you come down
coaching_cues: Grip a vertical pole, one hand high, one low
Press the bottom arm and pull with the top arm
Lift the body horizontal, legs together
common_mistakes: Skipping lead-ups and straining the shoulders
pro_tip: Train tucked and straddle versions before the full flag

name: Leg Pull in Flat Bench
breathing_cue: Exhale as the knees come in
coaching_cues: Lie on a flat bench, hands holding the sides
Pull the knees in toward your chest
Lower slowly without touching the floor
pro_tip: Curl the pelvis up at the top for more abs

name: Lying Leg Raise Flat Bench
breathing_cue: Exhale as the legs rise
coaching_cues: Lie on a flat bench, hold the edge behind you
Raise straight legs to about 90 degrees
Lower slowly, stop before the heels touch down
common_mistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the bench
pro_tip: Bend the knees slightly if the lower back complains

name: Kettlebell Single Arm Floor Press
breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Lie on the floor, bell held in the fist at the shoulder
Lower until the upper arm touches the floor
Press straight up, keeping the wrist stacked
common_mistakes: Letting the bell tip back and bend the wrist
Bouncing the elbow off the floor
pro_tip: Floor stops the elbow: a shoulder-friendly press

name: Cable Floor Seated Wide Grip Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you row, inhale on the return
coaching_cues: Sit on the floor, feet braced, chest tall
Pull the wide bar to the upper stomach, elbows flared
Squeeze the shoulder blades, then return slowly
common_mistakes: Rocking the torso back to heave the weight
Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
pro_tip: Wide grip shifts work to rear delts and mid back

name: Side Lying Floor Stretch
breathing_cue: Slow breaths, relax into the stretch on every exhale
coaching_cues: Lie on your side, legs stacked
Reach the top arm overhead and lengthen the side body
Hold without twisting the hips
common_mistakes: Rolling the hips forward or back
pro_tip: Reach farther by bending slightly the other way

name: Band Reverse Fly
breathing_cue: Exhale as the arms open, inhale on the return
coaching_cues: Hold the band at chest height, arms straight
Pull the hands apart, leading with the elbows
Squeeze the shoulder blades for a second
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows into a row
pro_tip: Use a lighter band and slow the return

name: Cable Incline Fly
breathing_cue: Exhale as the hands come together
coaching_cues: Lie on an incline bench between low cables
Open the arms wide with a slight elbow bend
Bring the hands together over the upper chest
common_mistakes: Turning it into a press by bending the elbows
Dropping the arms too far behind the shoulders
pro_tip: Set the bench at 30 degrees to target the upper chest

name: Dumbbell Decline Fly
breathing_cue: Inhale as the arms open, exhale as they close
coaching_cues: Lie on a decline bench, dumbbells over the chest
Lower in a wide arc with soft elbows
Squeeze the weights back together
common_mistakes: Going too heavy and bending the elbows
Dropping the arms below shoulder level
pro_tip: Hook your feet firmly so you stay on the bench

name: Dumbbell Decline Single Arm Fly
breathing_cue: Inhale as the arm opens, exhale as it closes
coaching_cues: Lie on a decline bench with one dumbbell
Open the working arm in a wide arc, soft elbow
Bring it back to the midline and squeeze
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso to cheat the rep
Letting the elbow bend into a press
pro_tip: Brace the core so the torso does not rotate

name: Dumbbell Incline Single Arm Fly
breathing_cue: Inhale as the arm opens, exhale as it closes
coaching_cues: Lie on an incline bench with one dumbbell
Open the working arm in a wide arc, soft elbow
Bring it back over the upper chest
common_mistakes: Straightening the elbow into a press
pro_tip: Keep the free arm out of the way or across the chest

name: Machine Seated Reverse Fly
breathing_cue: Exhale as you open the arms
coaching_cues: Sit facing the pad, chest against it
Pull the handles back in a wide arc, elbows soft
Squeeze the rear delts, return slowly
common_mistakes: Letting the weight stack crash between reps
pro_tip: Lighter weight and higher reps work best for rear delts

name: Supported Dumbbell Single Arm Reverse Fly
breathing_cue: Exhale as the arm lifts
coaching_cues: Rest one hand or chest on a support, hinge forward
Raise the dumbbell out to the side, elbow soft
Lower under control, no swinging
common_mistakes: Using the lower back to heave the weight
pro_tip: Support removes lower-back fatigue so rear delts work

name: Forward Jump
breathing_cue: Exhale on take-off, inhale on a soft landing
coaching_cues: Squat and swing the arms back
Drive the arms forward and jump as far as you can
Land soft on bent knees and hold
common_mistakes: Letting the knees cave inward on landing
pro_tip: Walk back to the start so each jump is fresh

name: Dumbbell Contralateral Forward Lunge
breathing_cue: Inhale on the step, exhale as you drive up
coaching_cues: Hold a dumbbell on the side opposite the front leg
Step forward and lower until both knees are about 90 degrees
Drive through the front heel to stand
common_mistakes: Letting the torso twist toward the weight
pro_tip: The opposite-side load makes the core and glute medius work

name: Forward Lunge
breathing_cue: Inhale as you lunge, exhale as you push back
coaching_cues: Step forward and drop the back knee toward the floor
Keep the front shin vertical and torso tall
Push off the front foot to return
common_mistakes: Front knee drifting past the toes and caving in
Short step with the heel lifting
pro_tip: Alternate legs or finish all reps on one side
indian_alternative: Use a dupatta on the floor as a step-length marker

name: Frankenstein Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Hold the barbell on straight arms out in front, like a zombie
Sit the hips back and down, chest tall
Drive up through the whole foot
pro_tip: Extended arms act as a counterweight for depth

name: Frog Planche
breathing_cue: Steady shallow breaths, do not hold
coaching_cues: Squat down, hands on the floor with fingers turned out
Rest knees on the elbows and lean forward
Lift the feet off the floor and hold
common_mistakes: Letting the shoulders sink between the hands
pro_tip: Warm up the wrists thoroughly before holds

name: Barbell Rollout From Bench
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull the bar back in
coaching_cues: Kneel at the end of a bench, hands on a loaded bar
Roll the bar forward with a tight, hollow body
Pull back using the abs, not the hips
common_mistakes: Rolling out farther than you can control
pro_tip: Start with short rollouts and add range weekly

name: Weighted Front Plank
breathing_cue: Breathe steadily, do not hold your breath
coaching_cues: Plank on forearms with a plate resting on the upper back
Keep a straight line from head to heels
Squeeze glutes and abs the whole time
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag or pike
Using a plate that makes you arch the back
pro_tip: Have a partner place the plate so it does not slide

name: Machine Front Pulldown
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull down, inhale as the bar rises
coaching_cues: Sit with thighs under the pads, chest tall
Pull the handles to the upper chest, elbows down
Return slowly to a full stretch
common_mistakes: Leaning back to swing the weight
Pulling with the arms instead of the lats
pro_tip: Think elbows to the hips, not hands to the chest

name: Band Front Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you raise
coaching_cues: Stand on the band, hold the other end in front
Raise straight arms to shoulder height
Lower slowly against the band tension
common_mistakes: Raising the arms above shoulder height
pro_tip: Step wider on the band to raise the resistance

name: Barbell Front Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as the bar rises
coaching_cues: Hold the bar shoulder-width in front of the thighs
Raise it to shoulder height with soft elbows
Lower slowly without swinging
common_mistakes: Leaning back to throw the bar up
Raising the bar above eye level
pro_tip: Use an EZ bar or light plates to keep form strict

name: Dumbbell Lateral to Front Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as the arms rise
coaching_cues: Raise the dumbbells out to the side to shoulder height
Lower, then raise them forward to shoulder height
Alternate the two, keeping the torso still
common_mistakes: Swinging the body to get the weights up
pro_tip: Go lighter than a normal lateral raise

name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Front Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as each arm rises
coaching_cues: Sit tall on a bench or chair, dumbbells at thighs
Raise one arm to shoulder height, then lower
Alternate arms without leaning back
common_mistakes: Raising the arm above shoulder height
pro_tip: Seated position removes leg drive and keeps it strict

name: Dumbbell Seated Front Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as the arms rise
coaching_cues: Sit tall on a bench or chair, dumbbells at thighs
Raise both arms to shoulder height together
Lower with control
common_mistakes: Leaning back to swing the weights
Raising the arms above shoulder height
pro_tip: Keep a slight elbow bend to protect the elbows

name: Barbell Bench Front Squat
breathing_cue: Brace before you sit, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Rack the bar on the front delts, elbows high
Sit back to lightly touch the bench
Stand without rocking, chest upright
common_mistakes: Collapsing the chest onto the bench
Dropping the elbows and losing the bar
pro_tip: Bench sets a consistent depth every rep

name: Barbell Clean Grip Front Squat
breathing_cue: Brace before you descend, exhale on the drive
coaching_cues: Clean grip, bar resting on the front delts, elbows high
Squat to at least parallel with a tall torso
Drive up leading with the chest
common_mistakes: Dropping the elbows and losing the rack
Knees caving in on the way up
pro_tip: Strap or lighten the grip if the wrists are stiff

name: Kettlebell Front Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Hold a kettlebell in each hand, racked at the chest
Sit down between the hips with an upright torso
Drive up through the heels
common_mistakes: Letting the bell pull the chest forward
pro_tip: Two kettlebells in the rack make it a serious leg day

name: Smith Machine Clean Grip Front Squat
breathing_cue: Brace before the descent, exhale on the drive
coaching_cues: Place feet slightly forward of the bar
Rest the bar on the front delts, elbows up
Squat down and drive up keeping the torso tall
common_mistakes: Feet directly under the bar, loading the knees
pro_tip: Smith machine front squat is easier to balance

name: Full Maltese
breathing_cue: Steady shallow breaths, avoid the breath hold
coaching_cues: Hold a full planche first, then widen the arms outward
Keep the body completely straight and parallel to the floor
Press the hands down and protract hard
common_mistakes: Rushing to it without years of planche base
Overloading the biceps tendons by skipping progressions
pro_tip: Elite skill; most athletes never need it

name: Full Planche
breathing_cue: Steady shallow breaths, avoid the breath hold
coaching_cues: Lean far forward on locked straight arms
Lift hips and legs into a straight body line
Squeeze glutes and abs, protract the shoulders
common_mistakes: Bending the arms or piking the hips
pro_tip: Build tuck then straddle planche before attempting full

name: Smith Full Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you drive up
coaching_cues: Place the bar on the upper back, feet slightly forward
Sit down and back to at least parallel
Drive through the whole foot to stand
common_mistakes: Heels lifting and the torso folding forward
pro_tip: Feet slightly forward of the bar spare the knees

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
breathing_cue: Exhale hard as you drive the hips up
coaching_cues: Sit with upper back against the floor or bench, bar over the hips
Plant feet flat and drive the hips up
Squeeze the glutes and hold the top for a second
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
Pushing through the toes instead of the heels
pro_tip: Pad the bar with a towel or foam wrap for comfort

name: Seated Glute Stretch
breathing_cue: Breathe slowly, sink deeper on each exhale
coaching_cues: Sit tall, cross one ankle over the opposite knee
Hinge forward from the hips with a flat back
Hold, then switch legs
pro_tip: Sit on a chair edge if the floor is too stiff

name: Lying Glutes Stretch
breathing_cue: Breathe slowly, relax into the stretch
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the opposite knee
Pull the thigh toward your chest with both hands
Hold, then switch sides
common_mistakes: Lifting the head and tensing the neck
Pulling hard on the knee joint
pro_tip: Keep the lower back flat on the floor

name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Hold the kettlebell by the horns at the chest
Sit down between your knees, elbows inside them
Drive up through the heels, chest tall
common_mistakes: Letting the bell pull the torso forward
pro_tip: Pause 1 second at the bottom to build control

name: Barbell Seated Good Morning
breathing_cue: Inhale as you hinge forward, exhale as you sit up
coaching_cues: Sit on a bench with the bar on the upper back
Hinge forward with a flat back, hips staying back
Sit up by squeezing the glutes and lower back
common_mistakes: Using too much weight too soon
pro_tip: Use only a light bar: this is a lower-back builder

name: Barbell Stiff Leg Good Morning
breathing_cue: Inhale as you hinge, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Bar on the upper back, legs nearly straight
Push the hips back and lower the torso with a flat spine
Squeeze the glutes to stand tall
pro_tip: Go only as low as your hamstrings allow with a flat back

name: Smith Bent Knee Good Morning
breathing_cue: Inhale as you hinge, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Set the bar on the upper back, knees softly bent
Push the hips back, keep a flat spine
Squeeze the glutes to stand up
common_mistakes: Letting the knees drift forward as you hinge
pro_tip: Bent knees make it glute-biased and easier on the hamstrings

name: Barbell Hack Squat
breathing_cue: Brace before you descend, exhale on the drive
coaching_cues: Hold the bar behind the legs, chest up
Squat down with heels flat, bar sliding down the legs
Drive up keeping the bar close to the calves
pro_tip: Heels slightly raised shifts the work to the quads

name: Smith Hack Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you push up
coaching_cues: Stand with the bar behind the thighs, heels together-ish
Sit down and back while the bar slides
Press up through the heels
pro_tip: Place the feet slightly forward to protect the knees

name: Half Pullup
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull up
coaching_cues: Hang from the bar and pull up about halfway
Keep shoulder blades pulled down
Lower slowly to a dead hang
common_mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders to the ears
pro_tip: Use as a bridge toward full pull-ups

name: Machine Glute Ham Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Hip pad under the pelvis, feet locked in
Lower the torso with a straight spine
Pull up with the hamstrings and glutes
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
pro_tip: Cross arms on chest to make it harder

name: Dumbbell Alternate Seated Hammer Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Sit tall with palms facing in
Curl one dumbbell up, then the other
Keep the elbows pinned to the sides
pro_tip: Alternate arms to keep tension longer

name: Dumbbell Cross Body Hammer Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Stand with palms facing in
Curl the dumbbell diagonally across the body
Keep the upper arm still
pro_tip: Aim toward the opposite shoulder for more brachialis

name: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Lie back on an incline bench, arms hanging
Curl with palms facing in
Keep the upper arms behind the torso
pro_tip: The long stretch at the bottom builds the biceps

name: Dumbbell Preacher Hammer Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Rest the upper arm on the preacher pad
Curl with a neutral grip, thumbs up
Lower fully without slamming at the bottom
common_mistakes: Lifting the elbows off the pad
pro_tip: Do not fully lock out the bottom if elbows feel sore

name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Hammer Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Lie chest-down on an incline bench, arms hanging
Curl with a neutral grip
Squeeze at the top without swinging
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad
pro_tip: Chest support removes cheating completely

name: Dumbbell Seated Hammer Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Sit tall on a bench or chair, palms facing in
Curl both dumbbells up, elbows pinned
Lower under control to full extension
pro_tip: Seated position stops hip drive and swinging

name: Dumbbell Single Arm Seated Hammer Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Sit tall, one dumbbell with palm facing in
Curl up, elbow pinned to the side
Lower under control
pro_tip: Use the free hand to check the elbow stays still

name: Dumbbell Single Arm Standing Hammer Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Stand tall, one dumbbell with palm facing in
Curl up, elbow pinned to the side
Lower under control
pro_tip: Brace the abs so the torso stays still

name: Dumbbell Decline Hammer Press
breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Lie on a decline bench, palms facing each other
Lower the dumbbells to the lower chest
Press up and squeeze the chest
common_mistakes: Bouncing the weights off the chest
pro_tip: Neutral grip is gentler on the shoulders

name: Dumbbell Decline Single Arm Hammer Press
breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Lie on a decline bench, one dumbbell, palm in
Lower to the side of the lower chest
Press up without twisting the torso
pro_tip: Brace the core to resist rotation

name: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Press
breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Lie on an incline bench, palms facing each other
Lower the dumbbells to the upper chest
Press up and squeeze the chest
pro_tip: Neutral grip is gentler on the shoulders

name: Dumbbell Incline Single Arm Hammer Press
breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Lie on an incline bench, one dumbbell, palm in
Lower to the side of the upper chest
Press up without twisting the torso
pro_tip: Brace the core to resist rotation

name: Dumbbell Lying Hammer Press
breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, palms facing each other
Lower the dumbbells beside the chest
Press up and squeeze the chest
pro_tip: Neutral grip keeps the shoulders happy

name: Dumbbell Lying Hamstring Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl the heels up
coaching_cues: Lie face down, dumbbell clamped between the feet
Curl the weight toward the glutes
Lower slowly without arching the back
common_mistakes: Lifting the hips off the bench
Dropping the dumbbell on the way down
pro_tip: Ask a partner to place the dumbbell between your feet

name: Leg Up Hamstring Stretch
breathing_cue: Breathe slowly, relax as you exhale
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, one leg raised straight
Hold behind the thigh or calf and gently pull
Keep the other leg and lower back flat
common_mistakes: Bending the raised knee too much
Lifting the hips off the floor
pro_tip: Loop a towel around the foot if you cannot reach
indian_alternative: Use a dupatta or towel around the foot

name: Hamstring Walkout
breathing_cue: Exhale as you walk the feet back in
coaching_cues: Lie on your back in a glute bridge, hips high
Walk the heels out slowly keeping the hips lifted
Walk back in under control
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag as the feet move out
Walking out so far that the hamstrings cramp
pro_tip: Use a shorter walk if the hamstrings cramp

name: Kettlebell Alternating Hang Clean
breathing_cue: Exhale sharply as the bell rises
coaching_cues: Hinge back, bell swinging between the legs
Snap the hips and pull the bell to the rack
Let it settle softly, then switch hands
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arm instead of the hips
Letting the bell slam into the forearm
pro_tip: Keep the elbow close and wrap the bell around the wrist

name: Kettlebell Double Alternating Hang Clean
breathing_cue: Exhale sharply as the bells rise
coaching_cues: Hinge back, a bell in each hand
Snap the hips and bring one bell to the rack, then alternate
Keep the torso upright and the bells close
pro_tip: Master the single-bell version first

name: Kettlebell Hang Clean
breathing_cue: Exhale sharply as the bell rises
coaching_cues: Hinge back, bell swinging between the legs
Snap the hips and pull the bell to the rack
Let it settle softly at the chest
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arm instead of the hips
Letting the bell slam into the forearm
pro_tip: Keep the elbow close and wrap the bell around the wrist

name: Kettlebell Bottoms Up Clean From the Hang Position
breathing_cue: Exhale as the bell rises, brace the core
coaching_cues: Swing the bell back and pull it up with the bottom facing up
Keep the wrist stacked and gripped hard
Control it at the chest in the rack position
common_mistakes: Letting the bell flip and slam the forearm
Using the arm instead of the hips
pro_tip: Great for grip and shoulder stability, use a light bell

name: Hanging Pike
breathing_cue: Exhale as the legs rise
coaching_cues: Hang from the bar, legs straight together
Pike the hips and lift the toes toward the bar
Lower slowly without swinging
pro_tip: Do hanging knee raises first if you cannot keep the legs straight

name: Alternate Heel Touchers
breathing_cue: Breathe out as you reach each side
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat
Lift the shoulders slightly and reach to touch one heel
Alternate sides without dropping the head
common_mistakes: Moving the hips instead of crunching sideways
pro_tip: Keep the shoulders lifted between reps for constant tension

name: Kettlebell Sumo High Pull
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull up
coaching_cues: Wide stance, hold the bell with both hands between the feet
Drive up through the legs and hips
Pull the bell to chin height, elbows high and wide
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms before the hips
Rounding the back at the bottom
pro_tip: Hips drive, arms guide

name: Cable Seated High Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull to the face
coaching_cues: Sit tall, cable set above chest height
Pull the handle toward the upper chest or face, elbows high
Squeeze the shoulder blades, return slowly
common_mistakes: Leaning back to swing the weight
pro_tip: Elbows high hits the rear delts and upper back

name: Cable Single Arm Kneeling High Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull

Lower with control

Press up keeping the back close to the bench

pro_tip: Bend the knees to ease it; straighten legs to progress.

Return slowly to the start

pro_tip: Use a light dumbbell, held near the end of the handle.

name: Dumbbell Lying Supination on Floor

coaching_cues: Lie down, elbow fixed, hold the dumbbell vertical
Rotate the palm slowly to face up
Return slowly to the start
common_mistakes: Using a weight too heavy to control
Letting the elbow move off the support
pro_tip: Use a light dumbbell, held near the end of the handle.

name: Kettlebell Alternating Press on Floor
breathing_cue: Exhale pressing up
coaching_cues: Lie on the floor, knees bent, kettlebell at the shoulder
Press one arm up while the other rests
Lower until the elbow touches the floor
common_mistakes: Letting the wrist bend back under the bell
Rolling the shoulder off the floor
pro_tip: Keep the bell resting on the forearm, wrist straight.

name: V-sit on Floor
breathing_cue: Breathe steadily through the hold
coaching_cues: Sit tall, lean back slightly, lift straight legs
Balance on the sit bones with the chest open
Reach the arms parallel to the legs
common_mistakes: Bending the knees to hold the position
pro_tip: Start with bent knees (tuck V-sit) and straighten over weeks.

name: Calf Press on Leg Press
breathing_cue: Exhale pushing up, inhale lowering
coaching_cues: Sit with only the balls of the feet on the platform
Press up high onto the toes, pause, squeeze
Lower for a full calf stretch
common_mistakes: Short range instead of full stretch and squeeze
pro_tip: Pause one second at both ends.

name: Calf Raise on Leg Press

coaching_cues: Sit with only the balls of the feet on the platform
Press up high onto the toes, pause, squeeze
Lower for a full calf stretch
common_mistakes: Short range instead of full stretch and squeeze
pro_tip: Pause one second at both ends.

name: Seated Squat Calf Raise on Leg Press Machine
breathing_cue: Exhale pushing up, inhale lowering
coaching_cues: Knees stay bent, balls of the feet on the platform
Press up high onto the toes, pause, squeeze
Lower for a full soleus stretch
common_mistakes: Short range instead of full stretch and squeeze
pro_tip: Pause one second at both ends.

name: Single Leg Calf Press on Leg Press

pro_tip: Pause one second at both ends.

name: Walking on Incline Treadmill (Distance)

coaching_cues: Set a 8-12 percent incline and a brisk pace
Stand tall
Do not hold the rails
Swing the arms naturally
common_mistakes: Gripping the handrails and leaning back
Setting a pace so fast the form breaks
pro_tip: Incline walking spares the knees versus running.

name: Barbell Standing Front Raise Over Head
breathing_cue: Exhale raising, inhale lowering
coaching_cues: Stand tall, bar held shoulder-width overhand at the thighs
Raise the bar with straight arms to overhead
Lower slowly to the thighs
common_mistakes: Swinging with the hips and lower back
pro_tip: Use a light bar; stop at overhead only if the shoulders feel fine.

name: Standing Glute Kickback (Band)
breathing_cue: Exhale as you kick back
coaching_cues: Stand tall with the band looped round the ankles, hands on a wall for balance
Kick the working leg straight back and squeeze the glute at the top
Return slowly without arching the lower back
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to swing the leg higher
Rotating the hips open as the leg goes back
pro_tip: Keep the hips square to the wall; the glute does the lift, not the back.

name: Dumbbell Seated Bent Over Alternate Kickback
breathing_cue: Exhale as you extend the arm
coaching_cues: Upper arm pinned to your side, parallel to the floor
Straighten the elbow fully and squeeze the triceps
Return slowly without letting the elbow drop
common_mistakes: Swinging the weight with the shoulder
Letting the upper arm sag away from the torso
pro_tip: Keep the upper arm still; only the forearm moves.

name: Barbell Reverse Grip Bent Over Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Underhand grip shoulder-width, hinge to 45 degrees
Pull the bar to the lower ribs, elbows close
Lower under control to straight arms
common_mistakes: Jerking the weight up with the torso
pro_tip: Underhand grip brings in more lats and biceps.

name: Cable Single Arm Bent Over Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Hinge over, free hand braced on the thigh or bench
Pull the handle to the hip, squeeze the lat
Let the arm stretch fully before the next rep
common_mistakes: Jerking the weight up with the torso
pro_tip: Rotate the torso slightly to feel the full lat stretch.

name: Dumbbell Bent Over Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Hinge to about 45 degrees with a flat back
Pull the elbows back toward the hips, squeeze the shoulder blades
Lower under control to full arm extension
common_mistakes: Jerking the weight up with the torso
pro_tip: Brace hard before every rep; keep the torso angle fixed.

name: Smith Bent Over Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Hinge to 45 degrees, overhand grip on the Smith bar
Row the bar to the lower ribs
Lower under control to straight arms
common_mistakes: Jerking the weight up with the torso
pro_tip: Brace hard before every rep; keep the torso angle fixed.

name: Smith Reverse Grip Bent Over Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Underhand grip, hinge to 45 degrees
Row the bar to the lower ribs, elbows tight
Lower under control to straight arms
common_mistakes: Jerking the weight up with the torso
pro_tip: Brace hard before every rep; keep the torso angle fixed.

name: Dumbbell Single Arm Overhead Carry
breathing_cue: Breathe steadily; keep the ribs down
coaching_cues: Press the dumbbell overhead, biceps by the ear
Walk tall with the ribs stacked over the hips
Resist leaning away from the weight
common_mistakes: Leaning sideways to offset the load
Letting the elbow bend or the wrist collapse
pro_tip: Do both sides equally; start light.

name: Barbell Seated Overhead Press
breathing_cue: Inhale at the shoulders, exhale pressing up
coaching_cues: Ribs down, glutes tight, wrists over elbows
Press straight up to full lockout
Lower to chin or shoulder height under control
common_mistakes: Leaning back to push the weight up
Flaring the elbows far behind the body
pro_tip: Squeeze the glutes to stop the lower back arching.

name: Dumbbell Standing Alternate Overhead Press
breathing_cue: Inhale at the shoulders, exhale pressing up
coaching_cues: Ribs down, glutes tight, wrists over elbows
Press straight up to full lockout
Lower to chin or shoulder height under control
common_mistakes: Leaning back to push the weight up

pro_tip: Squeeze the glutes to stop the lower back arching.

name: Squat to Overhead Reach
breathing_cue: Inhale reaching up, exhale squatting
coaching_cues: Feet shoulder-width, sink into a deep squat
Stand up and reach tall overhead
Keep the heels down and chest open
common_mistakes: Rounding the back in the squat
pro_tip: Hold a pole or door frame if balance is shaky.

name: Barbell Overhead Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale and brace before descent, exhale on the way up
coaching_cues: Wide snatch grip, bar locked out over the mid-foot
Squat deep while pressing the bar apart overhead
Keep the chest up and the bar stacked
common_mistakes: Bar drifting forward over the toes
Losing shoulder lockout at the bottom
pro_tip: Practice with a PVC pipe before loading.

name: Medicine Ball Catch and Overhead Throw
breathing_cue: Exhale sharply on the throw
coaching_cues: Catch the ball and absorb into a quarter squat
Extend hips and arms to throw overhead explosively
Reset fully before the next rep
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back on the throw
Throwing without a partner or wall target
pro_tip: Use a light ball and a rebounding wall.

name: Band Vertical Pallof Press
breathing_cue: Exhale pressing out
coaching_cues: Stand sideways to the anchor, band at chest
Press the hands up and out overhead without rotating
Return slowly and keep the hips square
common_mistakes: Letting the torso twist toward the anchor
pro_tip: Step further from the anchor for more tension.

name: Kettlebell Lunge Pass Through
breathing_cue: Inhale stepping, exhale pushing up
coaching_cues: Step into a lunge and pass the bell under the front thigh
Keep the chest tall and the front knee over the foot
Drive up and pass the bell back
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the bell
pro_tip: Practise the lunge unloaded first.

name: Back Pec Stretch
breathing_cue: Slow deep breaths; exhale to ease deeper
coaching_cues: Stand tall, clasp the hands behind the back
Straighten the arms and lift them slightly
Open the chest and hold
pro_tip: Squeeze the shoulder blades together as you lift.

name: Pelvic Tilt
breathing_cue: Exhale as you flatten the back, inhale as you release
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat
Tilt the pelvis to press the lower back into the floor
Hold briefly, then release
common_mistakes: Pushing with the legs instead of the abs
pro_tip: Think of zipping the belly button toward the spine.

name: Standing Pelvic Tilt
breathing_cue: Exhale as you tuck, inhale as you release
coaching_cues: Stand tall with knees soft, back against a wall if helpful
Tuck the pelvis to flatten the lower back
Release slowly to neutral
pro_tip: Try it with your back against a wall first.

name: Peroneals Stretch
breathing_cue: Slow deep breaths; exhale to ease deeper
coaching_cues: Sit with one knee bent and a band looped round that foot
Press gently on the outer foot and hold
Keep the ankle relaxed
pro_tip: Keep the band loose on the foot and pull it gently toward you.

name: Kettlebell Pistol Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale on the drive up
coaching_cues: Hold the bell at the chest as a counterweight
Sit down on one leg, other leg extended forward
Drive through the whole foot to stand
pro_tip: Use the bell as a counterbalance to help depth.

name: Dumbbell Plyo Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale as you jump
coaching_cues: Hold light dumbbells at the sides, squat to parallel
Jump explosively, fully extending the hips
Land softly into the next squat
pro_tip: Keep the dumbbells light; speed matters more than load.

name: Power Point Plank

coaching_cues: High plank on the hands with a rigid straight line
Squeeze glutes and brace the abs hard
Hold without letting the hips sag
pro_tip: Stop the set when form breaks, not when you are tired.

Lower until the knees reach about 90 degrees
Press through the whole foot
Do not lock the knees

Rack the bar when done
common_mistakes: Setting the bench too far from the bar path
pro_tip: Reverse grip is hard on the wrists; start light.
